setup.title: Your own Google app for Sheets
outcome: A Google Cloud project that belongs to the person's own Google account
The Google Sheets API is enabled in that project
An OAuth client of type Desktop app (never Web application), with no redirect URI added

The person's own Google address is allowed to sign in: while the app is in Testing it must be listed as a test user; once the app is In production, or the person uses Workspace 'Internal', no test-user list is needed

The app's publishing status is 'In production' (or the person uses Workspace 'Internal'), set BEFORE the person signs in. Never leave it in 'Testing': a Testing app's sign-in expires after 7 days, which would stop an unattended assistant every week
The console's 'AI-powered agent' option is left unchecked

The person is told in advance what an own app that is In production but not verified shows: the console says 'Your app requires verification' and the person does not need to submit the app for review; the sign-in page says 'Google hasn't verified this app', where the person chooses 'Advanced' and then 'Go to <app name> (unsafe)'. That is expected for their own app, not an error
steps: Open https://console.cloud.google.com/ and sign in with the person's own Google account. Accept Google's terms if asked. Nothing here needs a card or any payment: if Google asks for one, stop and ask the person to check with you before entering anything.
Create a project: open the project picker at the top, choose New project, give it a name such as TaskFollow Sheets, press Create, then make sure that project is the selected one.
Turn on the Google Sheets API: open APIs & Services, then Library, search for Google Sheets API, open it and press Enable. Enable nothing else.

Set up the consent screen (newer consoles call it Google Auth Platform): choose the user type External (a Google Workspace organisation may choose Internal), enter an app name such as TaskFollow, the person's email as support email and again as developer contact, and save.
Optional: on Data access (or Scopes), add the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets. TaskFollow asks for this scope only.

Set the app to In production before the person signs in: open Audience (or the consent screen's publishing status) and press Publish app or Make external, and confirm. Google then says 'Your app requires verification'; the person does not need to submit it. Never leave it in Testing, because a Testing sign-in stops working after 7 days.

Create the sign-in client: open Credentials (or Google Auth Platform, then Clients), choose Create credentials, then OAuth client ID, and choose the application type Desktop app (never Web application). Give it a name and press Create. Add no redirect address. If the console offers to use the client for an AI-powered agent, leave that unchecked.
Copy the Client ID and the Client secret from the window that appears (each has a copy icon beside it). The person keeps them for the next step and never types them into the chat.

Run the sign-in command the install names (taskfollow secret google). On the page that opens, the person pastes the Client ID and the Client secret, then allows access on Google's page. Google shows 'Google hasn't verified this app': they choose Advanced, then Go to the app (unsafe). The page says Done when it worked.

symptoms.means: The OAuth client is the wrong type
symptoms.fix: Create a new client of type Desktop app; a Web application client cannot be used.
symptoms.look: In the Google Cloud console, open the project's Credentials page and read the 'Type' column of the client.
symptoms.search: Google OAuth redirect_uri_mismatch desktop app client type

symptoms.means: Google did not grant access: the person pressed Deny, or this address may not sign in to the app yet
symptoms.fix: Sign in again and press Allow on Google's page. If it still fails and the app is in Testing, add the address as a test user on the consent screen; if the app is in production, read Google's message word for word.
symptoms.look: Open the consent screen settings (called 'Audience' in newer consoles) and check the publishing status and the list of test users.
symptoms.search: Google OAuth access_denied app not verified test users

symptoms.means: The client ID or secret is wrong
symptoms.fix: Copy both again from the client's page and enter them on the sign-in page.
symptoms.look: Open the client's page under Credentials and compare the client ID with what was typed.
symptoms.search: Google OAuth invalid_client client ID secret

symptoms.means: Google refused the sign-in: a one-time code that was used twice or expired, or a stored sign-in that was revoked or expired
symptoms.fix: If it keeps happening about every 7 days, the app is still in Testing status: switch it to In production first, then sign in again. Otherwise sign in again.
symptoms.look: Open the consent screen settings and read the publishing status; check https://myaccount.google.com/connections to see whether the app's access was removed.
symptoms.search: Google OAuth refresh token expires 7 days testing publishing status

symptoms.means: The Google Sheets API is not enabled in the project
symptoms.fix: Enable the Google Sheets API in the same Google Cloud project, then verify again.
symptoms.look: In the Google Cloud console open 'APIs & Services' and check that the Google Sheets API shows as enabled for this project.
symptoms.search: enable Google Sheets API Google Cloud project

symptoms.means: Access to Google Sheets was not allowed when signing in
symptoms.fix: Sign in again with 'taskfollow secret google' and leave the Google Sheets box ticked on Google's page.
symptoms.look: On Google's sign-in page, check that the permission about Google Sheets spreadsheets is ticked before pressing Continue.

symptoms.means: The administrator of the person's work or school Google account does not allow this app, or does not allow making Google Cloud projects
symptoms.fix: Use a personal Google account (an address ending in gmail.com) for this setup, or ask the administrator to allow the app and to let you create Google Cloud projects.
symptoms.look: Read the message on Google's page word for word: it names the policy that blocked the app.
symptoms.search: Google Workspace admin_policy_enforced OAuth app blocked administrator
